author: reek
body: The counter-latch command, pinned by the one property that distinguishes it from its absence.

author: reek
body: The obvious test -- latch, read both halves, check they agree -- passes against a machine with no latch at all. The counter moves between the two reads either way, and two bytes sampled a microsecond apart almost always look like a coherent pair. A check that passes on a controller that does nothing is not a check.

author: reek
body: What a latch actually promises is that the value goes STALE: once frozen, it must not follow the counter. So the test reads a coherent value, latches, lets a lot of time pass, and then reads the latch. A working latch answers the value from before the delay. A missing one answers the value from after it -- which is exactly what the live counter says, and that is the tell.

author: reek
body: Read the frozen value WITHOUT latching first, so the delay sits between the latch and the read. This is the call whose answer the whole test turns on.

author: reek
body: The delay is measured, not counted. A fixed spin of N iterations takes whatever wall time the host happens to give it, which put the elapsed count either side of the threshold depending on machine load -- a flaky test, and a flaky test is worth less than none.

author: reek
body: Fuel-capped: a channel that never advances ends the wait instead of hanging the machine, and the verdict then reports a delay that did not happen.

author: reek
body: The local APIC timer divides an input frequency that nothing had ever measured or advertised. A guest could rely on the period scaling with the initial count and the divisor, and on nothing else -- so a guest calibrating the LAPIC against the PIT had no way to know whether the two clocks agreed about how fast a second is. This measures it: count LAPIC ticks against PIT ticks and work back to the input frequency.

author: reek
body: The timer is armed MASKED, so it counts without delivering an interrupt and the boot processor's own PIT-driven scheduling is left alone.
